title: Dietary energy restriction and weight-loss maintenance
question: Does this candidate engage the approved PM8 endocrine operation at its claimed exposure and evidential level?

relationship_assessment.type_b: Independent intervention admission: measured PM-specific local response within defined protocol/context.
relationship_assessment.delivery: Direct relative to measured local adipose response; no intermediary dietary precursor is asserted.

reason: Supports bounded dietary-programme SOP, not universal hormone optimisation. Release subgroup n=27, expression n=42. No untreated comparator for pooled analysis; exercise could not be isolated. Whole-tissue ex vivo release is not in vivo flux. Population, depot, weight loss and energy balance constrain interpretation. Independent qualified support for dietary programme; retain null adiponectin result. No weight-stable comparator; cannot separate energy deficit from weight loss. Adiponectin null qualifies You abdominal response; no macronutrient superiority. Tested deficit is a study exposure, not an effective-dose prescription. Phase qualification of admitted dietary programme. Uncontrolled multiphase programme; cellular source and energy-balance phase matter. Does not justify sustained maximisation of leptin suppression or a general very-low-calorie diet recommendation.
resolution_criterion: Broader populations, weight-independent mediation and secretion/flux or receptor outcomes would extend the current bounded admission.

source_assessments.title: Regional adipose tissue hormone/cytokine production before and after weight loss in abdominally obese women.
source_assessments.label: You et al. (2014)
source_assessments.exposure: 42 older abdominally obese women; 20-week hypocaloric programme, with or without aerobic exercise; pooled pre/post analysis. Ex vivo release measured in 27 women.
source_assessments.endpoint: Abdominal/gluteal tissue leptin and adiponectin gene expression and ex vivo release; plasma separately.
source_assessments.result: Weight loss 10.1 ± 0.7 kg. Leptin release decreased in both depots; adiponectin release increased only abdominally. Tissue and circulating changes were not significantly correlated.
source_assessments.limitations: Release subgroup n=27, expression n=42. No untreated comparator for pooled analysis; exercise could not be isolated. Whole-tissue ex vivo release is not in vivo flux. Population, depot, weight loss and energy balance constrain interpretation.
source_assessments.decision: Supports bounded dietary-programme SOP, not universal hormone optimisation.
source_assessments.access: Full primary Methods/Results/Discussion and figures recovered through Scite; all 21,177 body characters reviewed.

source_assessments.title: Effects of different hypocaloric diets on protein secretion from adipose tissue of obese women.
source_assessments.label: Arvidsson et al. (2004)
source_assessments.exposure: 40 women with obesity randomised to 10-week hypocaloric low-fat/high-carbohydrate or moderate-fat/moderate-carbohydrate diets; deficit 600 kcal/day.
source_assessments.endpoint: Subcutaneous adipose ex vivo protein secretion and transcripts, with circulating concentrations separately.
source_assessments.result: Approximately 7.5% weight loss and 40% lower leptin secretion; adiponectin secretion unchanged. Diet arms had similar responses.
source_assessments.limitations: No weight-stable comparator; cannot separate energy deficit from weight loss. Adiponectin null qualifies You abdominal response; no macronutrient superiority. Tested deficit is a study exposure, not an effective-dose prescription.
source_assessments.decision: Independent qualified support for dietary programme; retain null adiponectin result.
source_assessments.access: Primary abstract and accessible journal/PDF excerpts; complete bias appraisal remains limited.

source_assessments.exposure: 48 women with obesity: 1-month very-low-calorie diet then 5 months stabilisation/maintenance; release subgroup 26, transcript subgroup 22.

source_assessments.label: Stomby et al. (2015)
source_assessments.exposure: 49 postmenopausal women with overweight/obesity randomised to Paleolithic-type or Nordic-recommendation diets for 24 months.
source_assessments.endpoint: Subcutaneous adipose 11β-HSD1 mRNA, hepatic cortisone conversion and systemic metabolites.
source_assessments.result: Adipose 11β-HSD1 mRNA decreased at 6 and 24 months while weight fell; hepatic conversion increased transiently at 6 months.
source_assessments.limitations: Transcript is not local enzyme activity or cortisol-regeneration flux. Both diets produced weight loss; no independent effect of individual foods or weight-independent mechanism. Published 2015, online 2014.
source_assessments.decision: Relevant local transcript evidence; retain contrast with Tomlinson and systemic Stimson null without claiming all dietary engagement absent.
source_assessments.access: Primary abstract and metadata; full methods not independently recovered
